- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, then gradually decline — suggesting lagged reaction to true market dynamics.
- After a spike in forecast (e.g., >75), true values often drop sharply, indicating model fails to capture short-term volatility or policy-driven corrections.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds high values longer than observed in true data.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, especially when recent history includes downward trends.
- Model reacts too slowly to downward momentum in history — fails to adjust forecast mean downward when recent prices are falling.
- Overshoots are more common in the first 10–15 days of forecast horizon, then gradually correct — suggesting model lacks adaptive smoothing.
- When true values dip below 60, model often fails to recognize the trend and continues to forecast above 65–70.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of downward corrections after spikes — e.g., forecast 75, true 60–65, but model doesn’t adjust enough.
- Forecasts are too smooth — fail to capture abrupt drops or spikes in true data, especially in the last 5–7 days of the 30d window.
